title: Symmetric algebra, canonical inclusion and induced algebra map
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and $M$ an $R$-module. Using $R$-algebras and their homomorphisms [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient], define $\operatorname{Sym}_R(M)$ to be the tensor algebra $T_R(M)$ modulo the ideal generated by $\iota(v)\iota(w)-\iota(w)\iota(v)$ for $v,w\in M$. Here $T_R(M)$ is the free associative unital $R$-algebra generated $R$-linearly by $M$. Write $\iota:M\to\operatorname{Sym}_R(M)$ for the canonical $R$-linear inclusion into the quotient. For a commutative $R$-algebra $A$ and an $R$-linear map $g:M\to A$, define $\operatorname{lift}(g):\operatorname{Sym}_R(M)\to A$ by descending the tensor-algebra map which sends each generator $m$ to $g(m)$; commutativity of $A$ kills the displayed relations. This is the canonical algebra homomorphism used to induce maps between symmetric algebras.
